correctness.rationale: For any chosen bipartition class X and opposite class Y, parity restricts unselected vertices to one class. Any Y-Y pair has an even-length geodesic and unique midpoint v. If v in X it witnesses equality; if v in Y and degree(v)>=3, an off-geodesic X-neighbor witnesses equality. For a degree-two v in Y with both X-neighbors nonleaves, choose Y vertices two steps down each branch: v is their unique equalizer and lies outside X. If every degree-two Y-vertex has a leaf neighbor, this obstruction cannot arise, proving both directions. Bipartition containment forces the sharpness equivalence. When both classes work, upward closure plus inclusion-exclusion proves the complete polynomial. Independent code: C++ 18,748 tested tree instances and Python 1,616.

originality.rationale: The 2021 foundation proves the bipartite-class containment lower bound but not its sharpness characterization for all trees; the 2026 balanced three-edge spider record studies one special strict-gap family, and the 2026 community tree-counterexample uses only a midpoint obstruction. The iff local criterion across all trees and the full shape-independent polynomial for the precisely characterized subclass are not logically entailed by these cited statements without an additional universal off-path witness argument. Actual published-finding corpus queries and public source inspections are documented; unindexed equivalents remain a risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or alternate-name priority in finite-tree distance-equalizer literature cannot be fully excluded.

The earlier known parity and unique-midpoint lemmas are close proof ingredients; the originality claim is confined to the stated global iff sharpness characterization and complete polynomial, not those lemmas.

value.rationale: A broad natural family of trees is treated exhaustively: an iff linear-time local test tells exactly when the foundational equidistant-dimension bipartite lower bound is attained in arbitrary trees, and an iff characterization gives a complete equidistant-set polynomial on the large leaf-guarded degree-two class (including all homeomorphically irreducible trees). The polynomial reveals shape-independence at fixed bipartition sizes. It is an infinite-family structural classification addressing a motivated gap, not an arbitrary finite slice or a known-table recomputation.
